measurement: MP-REL3 preview trace read natively after an accessibility invoke
result: InvokePattern.Invoke() on support-preview-button returned without an exception, yet the published trace stayed action=none;build=none;install=none;render=absent at 1.5 s, 3 s and 5 s. With no positive control showing a trace transition being read back through automation in this window, this is strong evidence that the action handler did not run, but it does not conclusively exclude the generation-side candidates (a task that never finishes, a completion rejected by the state machine). The earlier wording that excluded them is withdrawn.
what_remains_open: Two questions, in order: whether a trace transition can be read back through automation at all in this window (positive control), and why the accessibility action appears not to reach this element's handler while the diagnostics toggle is reached by the same mechanism.
not_claimed: No defect classification beyond the observation, no fix, and no claim that assistive technology users are affected on other builds; the earlier preview observation at ce14dca is still not reproduced here.

re_measurement_after_notify.result: With every trace update now followed by a repaint request, an invoke that returned cleanly still left action=none at 1.5 s, 3 s and 5 s. A missing repaint is therefore ruled out as the explanation, but this is not a positive control: notify is a repaint request, not a measurement that automation published the value, and nothing in this run shows a trace change being read back. action=none is strong evidence that the handler did not run; it does not conclusively exclude the generation-side candidates.
re_measurement_after_notify.still_open: Why dispatch might differ between the two elements is open, and so is whether a trace transition can be read back through automation at all in this window (positive control). Because that control is missing, the generation-side candidates are not excluded either; the observation that action=none persisted is evidence, not a conclusion about where the chain stops.

positive_control: ATTEMPTED AND NEGATIVE - see evidence-published/rel3-positive-control-20261104. A ValuePattern.SetValue that returned cleanly did not change the search value or the row list, so a successful accessibility call is not evidence that the handler ran, and action=none cannot be read as proof that the preview handler was not reached.
